CJ-15 is already a frozen local stress fixture; CJ-13 is still inference/window-gated.
findings.revised_deliverable: Add a deterministic, fixture-only structured-response adapter for the existing local second reader against the already-frozen CJ-15 cases. Reuse the existing typed output schema and repair/parse refusal behavior; preserve the same case order, gold criterion labels and invalid denominator. Show that resolved pairs, unresolved/failure counts, agreement, accuracy against frozen gold, and adjudication projection are separately computed. Do not change the live judge or declare the operational goal accepted until the existing MI210 window rerun.

toolkit_reuse.what: Current harness already freezes per-criterion expected labels, uses typed `Question`/`DecisionResult` for reader A, and parses free-form reader B; replace only the deterministic fixture path with the existing structured schema/repaired-output API and retain failure outcomes.
Use canonical constrained response shape instead of hand-rolled labels; test invalid/omitted verdicts as failures, never defaults.
Reuse typed failure/refusal representation and test via injected/mock response; do not launch a model.

source_evidence.observation: CJ-13 explicitly records the 63/72 parse failures, 9/72 resolved agreement denominator, and requires structured/repaired reader before the same-rubric comparison.
CJ-16 is separately a local cascade shadow with threshold/fallback/sequential-latency measurement and must not be conflated with CJ-13.
The existing harness has a typed reader, free-form JSON extraction, frozen expected criteria and explicit parse-failure records.
DecisionResult preserves decisions and ParseFailure rather than substituting a silent answer.

findings.non_inference_scope: Offline synthetic fixture tests with injected structured/malformed judge responses; no inference, benchmark window, live backend, or judge authority changes.
findings.inference_acceptance: CJ-13 itself remains gated on `GATE: mi210-window`; only after fixture acceptance should the same-rubric local comparison rerun. Report accuracy, pair agreement and disagreement-based adjudication separately.
findings.gate: MI210 measurement window per existing operator ruling; no new approval request for the offline code/fixture slice.
findings.ownership: Canonical judge suite owner; do not modify coherence_judge/calibration subsystem (parallel-owned). CJ-13 is the single owner of cheap-judge redundancy; CJ-16 stays separate.
findings.proposed_handoff_append: **Proposed JEV implementation refinement (no new task or warrant):** Before CJ-13’s existing `mi210-window` rerun, reuse `typed_decisions.schema` and the existing runner’s typed `DecisionResult`/`ParseFailure` semantics to make reader B emit a constrained structured verdict on the already-frozen CJ-15 rubric cases. Add mock-only conformance for valid verdicts, omitted/invalid outputs, and refusal; retain every invalid case in the denominator. Compute resolved-pair agreement separately from each reader’s accuracy against the frozen labels and from the disagreement-based adjudication projection. This closes only the local parse/fixture defect; the local model comparison, realized cost, and adoption remain under the existing CJ-13/CJ-GATE boundaries. No hosted Jev, no new grading ladder, and no model call in the fixture tests.
